html:
The Kazakh Khanate was founded in about 1465, when the sultans Kerei and Janibek led their followers away from Abu'l-Khayr Khan of the Uzbeks to the Chu valley in Semirechye, in what is now Kazakhstan.

Both were descendants of Genghis Khan through Jochi. Those who followed them came to be called Kazakhs, a word meaning free wanderers. Under Qasim Khan in the early 1500s the khanate grew into a great steppe power, controlling the lands from the Caspian to Semirechye.

Later the Kazakhs split into three hordes, or zhuz: Great, Middle and Little. Wars with the Dzungars in the 18th century brought the Years of Great Disaster, and Ablai Khan and others turned to Russia for help. Kazakhstan marked 550 years of Kazakh statehood in 2015.
